newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli-Palestinian meeting aims to end deadlock.
newsitem.headline: Israeli-Palestinian meeting aims to end deadlock.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy met senior PLO negotiator Nabil Shaath on Sunday as part of a European bid to advance stalled Israeli-PLO peace moves ahead of a European foreign ministers' meeting.

Miguel Moratinos, Europe's Middle East peace envoy, has been trying to get Israel and the PLO to agree on confidence building measures to pave the way for a possible meeting between Levy and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Brussels on Tuesday.

European officials voiced doubt Arafat would attend the 15-member European Union's General Affairs Council meeting but an aide to Levy said he hoped the foreign minister and the PLO leader would meet.
"We hope so, we'll see after the meeting," said the aide Freddy Eytan. Arafat's senior aide Nabil Abu Rdainah said the Palestinian president had not yet decided whether to attend the EU meeting.
Eytan said Sunday's meeting with Shaath would "first and foremost" focus on Israeli allegations that a senior Palestinian security official sent three police officers to attack Jews in the West Bank.

"This is an invitation from Ambassador Moratinos to me and Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy to discuss the upcoming meeting in Brussels," Shaath told reporters before the meeting joined by Moratinos.

Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali, meanwhile, met Arafat in the Palestinian self-ruled West Bank town of Ramallah to discuss boosting coordination and to review ways of breaking the impasse in Israeli-Palestinian peace talks.
On Saturday, senior Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said the United States was formulating an initiative to end the deadlock in peace talks with Israel.

He told Reuters by telephone from the United States that U.S. officials at the highest levels were preparing a "package deal" but would not reveal details to the parties involved until it had been worked out fully.
"The U.S. administration is studying and working on ideas to formulate an initiative to help restart peace talks," Erekat said on Saturday night.

Erekat said he had talks in Washington with U.S. Undersecretary of State Thomas Pickering, a key figure in the new initiative. Pickering also met Uzi Arad, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's political adviser, in Washington.

Peace negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians have been at a standstill since March when Israel began building a Jewish settlement on occupied land in Arab East Jerusalem. The Palestinians say they will not resume negotiations until Israel halts settlement building.

A Palestinian official said Arad proposed in Washington last week that a decades-old Israeli initiative known as the Allon plan could serve as the starting point for fresh talks. "I think Allon plus could be a basis for reviving the talks," he said.
Netanyahu outlined to his cabinet last month a final settlement plan, likened to the Allon plan, under which Israel would keep key areas of the occupied West Bank.

He has also suggested moving immediately to accelerated talks on the final status of the West Bank and Gaza Strip. Palestinians charge the proposal is a ploy to avoid carrying out existing peace deals, including further West Bank pullbacks.

"I told Mr Pickering that any U.S. package deal would have to include a pause in all settlement activities and that final status talks must take place parallel to implementation of outstanding interim issues," Erekat said.
